title: Reorderer insights and oncall tips — weekly writeup
content:
Summary
- Focus this week: prototype of the request reorderer that smooths micro-burst imbalances and reduces head-of-line blocking for high-variance sequences. Small rollout to night shift pool (n3) for 24h soak.
- Secondary: KV-cache eviction tuning (LRU-ish hybrid) after noticing 12% miss-rate spikes on long-chat workloads.
- Batching: introduced a soft deadline policy change (deadline=15ms -> 12ms on p99 latency-critical pools) to observe effect on throughput/latency tradeoff.

Standup highlights (10/12)
- Maya: deployed reorderer v0.1 to n3; initial observations show reduction in 95th latency for small-chat cohort (~9% improvement) but slight throughput regression on streaming-heavy workloads.
- Ethan: instrumented per-kernel timing for reorder shuffle step; saw CPU jitter when reorder buffer > 4k requests — need to cap buffer and fall back to passthrough.
- Lina: KV cache tuning branch merged to canary; eviction threshold adjusted from 0.78 -> 0.86 occupancy, which lowered eviction churn but increased memory pressure in worst-case; will add adaptive cap.
- Akira: updated batcher metrics to expose reorderer-accepted vs rejected counts and added a histogram for inter-arrival skew.

Data & quick numbers (soak window: 03:00–06:00 UTC on n3)
- Small-chat cohort p95 latency: baseline 124ms -> v0.1 113ms (~9% drop)
- Streaming-heavy cohort throughput: baseline 820 req/s -> v0.1 790 req/s (~3.7% drop)
- KV cache miss-rate daytime tail: 12.4% -> 9.2% after eviction tweak (canary)
- CPU for reorder shuffle step: median 6µs, 95th 1.8ms when buffer >4k

What we tried and why it mattered
- Reorderer: goal is to group requests by expected token-length and latency-sensitivity to form smoother batches without starving small-latency requests. Algorithm: lightweight scoring (recent-length-mean, latency_weight) + sliding window greedy pack. Chose greedy window for low lock contention.
- Observed pathological case: large streaming sessions that emit token-by-token created many small requests; reorderer tried to pack them and then the kernel suffered IO stalls. Temporary mitigation: classify streaming sessions (streaming=true) and route them around reorderer.
- KV cache: eviction churn caused by many ephemeral tiny contexts; bumping occupancy reduced churn but worsened memory pressure spikes on bursts. Plan: hybrid TTL for small keys (<128B) + occupancy heuristic.

Open questions / outstanding risks
- Reorderer fairness: how to avoid starvation for low-frequency but latency-critical customers? Current fairness uses per-tenant minimum acceptance rate, but configuration is manual. Need an SLA-driven autotuner.
- Kernel interaction: some kernels are sensitive to input ordering (tile-affinity); reorderer currently ignores kernel affinity. Risk: reorder can increase cache warmup for kernels preferred by specific request shapes.
- Operational SLOs: soft-deadline adjustments reduced p99 in some pools but caused 4% request drop on others; need clearer routing rules to keep SLAs intact.

Action items (owner, ETA)
- Ethan: cap reorder buffer at 4k and implement immediate passthrough fallback; add unit test for path where buffer overflows. ETA: 2029-10-15.
- Maya: implement tenant-minimum acceptance auto-config prototype (seed with top-30 tenants) and run canary. ETA: 2029-10-20.
- Lina: add hybrid TTL eviction experiment to canary branch and monitor memory tail for 48h. ETA: 2029-10-16.
- Akira: add dashboard panels: reorderer accept/reject by tenant, reorderer-induced kernel-miss rate, and per-kernel affinity collision alerts. ETA: 2029-10-17.
- Oncall playbook update: short section describing how to detect reorderer induced stalls (metric names and quick remedial commands). Owner: Maya. ETA: 2029-10-14.

Oncall tips (notes to first responders)
- Quick signals that reorderer is implicated: spike in kernel-load-ms but no corresponding infra-saturation (GPU util flat), increase in reorderer.rejected_count (canary) and reorderer.buffer-size > 4k.
- Quick mitigation commands:
  - Turn off reorderer on a pool: infra-tool set-pool-config --pool n3 --reorderer.enabled false
  - Lower reorder window: infra-tool set-pool-config --pool n3 --reorderer.window_ms 6
  - Force passthrough for streaming: infra-tool set-tenant-flag --tenant TID123 streaming_passthrough true
- If kernel affinity collisions suspected: enable kernel-affinity-debug (sampling 0.5%) and escalate to kernel team.

Notes to self / brainstorming (informal)
- Could we piggyback lightweight sketch of token-length distribution in client envelope to reduce reorderer guesswork? Privacy concerns but maybe safe if quantized buckets.
- Consider probabilistic acceptance rather than hard min-quotas for tenants to allow graceful degradation.
- Explore moving reorderer earlier into routing layer (region edge) to reduce cross-host shuffle costs; tradeoff: complexity and more routing hops.

Relevant links and traces (for post-mortem and deeper dive)
- GH PR: GH-interop/reorderer-proto-PR#842 (proto + tests)
- JIRA epic: SRV-1183 (reorderer + eviction experiments)
- Example trace: trace_id: rdo-20291012-9932 (spike capture with kernel timing and reorderer events)

Next sync (tentative)
- Thursday 2029-10-17 09:30 PT — 30m lab sync to review canary results and decide rollout or rollback.

Small wins and celebration
- Shoutout to Akira for fast instrumentation that made root-cause visible within 3h of rollout.
- Lina for spotting the eviction-churn pattern in dashboards during the first soak.

Unresolved / parking-lot
- SLA-driven autotuner design document (move to product backlog).
- Kernel affinity modelling (request from kernel-team).
